minor.comment: The Dispatcher Agent has its own Commands. `dispatcher.submit` submits one turn to the addressed Dispatcher's own Agent and `dispatcher.interrupt` interrupts it; both address that Dispatcher through the caller context, like every other Command in the namespace, and both are reachable over `admin.sock` and a Channel's in-process port. `team.submit` and `team.interrupt` now require `team_name`: a Team Command names exactly one Team, and a call that omits the name is answered `BAD_REQUEST` by schema validation before any Agent is reached, instead of silently reaching the Dispatcher Agent. A caller that relied on the omission calls the Dispatcher Command instead. The two submit Commands share one reader for the Channel-facing payload (`service/channel-submission.ts`), which owns the attribute, text, reminder, and `source_id` rules once and fixes the `channel` provenance for both, and `DispatcherService.interrupt(teamId | null)` splits into `interruptAgent()` and `interruptTeamLeader(teamId)` to match.
Support ultrathink through native Codex effort parameters, restore ordinary effort on the next ordinary submission, and pass submission text through unchanged. Busy input follows native Codex timing.

BREAKING: `dispatchers[].cwd` is now required and must be a non-empty string on every Dispatcher entry, enabled or not; a config without it fails to load with an error naming the Dispatcher id. Rebuild: add "cwd": "<absolute dir>" to every dispatchers[] entry that lacks it.

Refuse new Workflow TeamMate construction after its Team or Dispatcher starts closing, before allocating a name, workspace, identity, or launch hooks; preserve already-admitted construction cleanup and lock finalization.
Default omitted dispatcher workspace policies and new onboarding to false; preserve explicit values. Repository-free work uses the dispatcher cwd unless isolation is enabled.

Load plugins from an optional top-level `plugins[]` in `config.json` (`builtin:<id>` or `npm:<package>[#export]` refs, each a string or `{ ref, config }`); existing configs load unchanged. Plugins can contribute providers addressed as `builtin:<name>`, append instructions and skill roots to Dispatcher and TeamLeader launches, and react to Team creation; a failing plugin hook is logged and skipped. `dreamux doctor` lists loaded plugins and plugin load failures. Ships the built-in, opt-in `builtin:bootstrap` plugin, which injects `.workspace/identity.md` and `user.md` from the Dispatcher cwd.

Redact tool call invocations and arguments in the conversation projection. Secret masking and workspace/home path renaming now apply to every displayed member of a tool call, and a call's structured payloads are redacted by walking the JSON value, so a secret written into a nested object or a multi-line .env is masked and the payload is still valid JSON. The redaction rules themselves moved to @excitedjs/dreamux-utils, where the host logger and config display now share one list of secret key names; the logger previously missed api_key, private_key, and client_secret.

Code organization refactor stage 6d: scheduler/service.ts renamed to index.ts and scheduler/mcp-delegate.ts to mcp.ts (matching the agent/team/workflow-service per-domain template); a new requests.ts holds the request readers and result projections previously split across types.ts and store.ts, which is now persistence-only; the dead dispatcherId option/parameter was dropped from CronJobStore and detectLegacyCronJobStore; the fire path was consolidated onto one store read per fire plus a pure advanceJob/impure rearm pair (a one-shot job whose dispatch throws is now disabled immediately instead of staying enabled with a stale next_run_at until the next start()); and SchedulerService now implements SchedulerCommands directly, with TeamService composing its own closing fence directly into the admit closure it passes at construction instead of wrapping the public command surface in a second, Team-scoped object.

Codex and Claude Code now load exactly like the built-in Feishu plugin: both are always-loaded plugins that contribute their Agent Runtime provider, instead of a core-side static builtin-provider registry pre-registering their descriptors ahead of the provider loader importing their package. No behavior change for a default install: both still register under builtin:codex / builtin:claude-code before agents[] is resolved, and a config naming an unmapped builtin:<ref> still fails loud with the same UnknownBuiltinProviderPackageError it always has. `dreamux uninstall`'s directory-safety guard also no longer hard-codes ~/.codex and ~/.claude: it now builds the same always-loaded plugin registry and asks each registered Agent Runtime provider for its own operatorStateRoot, so a provider added or removed by future plugin work is protected (or not) automatically. The protected paths for a default install are unchanged.

BREAKING: code organization refactor stage 8c, item 1: `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR` is deleted, and so is `dreamux onboard`'s `--config-dir` option; `dreamux uninstall --config-dir` is deleted too, by inference — it has nothing left to relocate once `config.json` is root-derived. `config.json` now always lives at `<DREAMUX_ROOT>/config.json` (default `~/.dreamux/config.json`, unchanged only for an install that set neither `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR` nor `DREAMUX_ROOT`); the managed-service unit now writes `DREAMUX_ROOT` instead of `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR`, taking the value from the environment of the process that runs `dreamux daemon install` or `dreamux onboard` (`~/.dreamux` when unset); `dreamux uninstall` now also removes the whole root directory itself, not just its contents. Before this change `DREAMUX_ROOT` relocated only state, run, cache and logs, `config.json` came from `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/.dreamux`, and the managed-service unit that `dreamux daemon install` wrote carried no `DREAMUX_ROOT`, so a managed service ran with `.dreamux` under its `HOME` as its root unless its environment supplied a `DREAMUX_ROOT` by another route (a unit drop-in, an environment file, or the service manager's own environment). Scenario 1: an install that set `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR` to a path other than the root it ran with — after upgrade `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR` is silently ignored, so the daemon looks for `config.json` under the root instead of the operator's configured directory. If no `config.json` exists there, the daemon fails on an ordinary missing-file error that never mentions `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR` or what moved, and the unit's `Restart=on-failure` loops; if a `config.json` already exists there (for example from an earlier default-path `dreamux onboard`), the daemon starts silently against that unrelated file instead. Scenario 2: an operator who exports `DREAMUX_ROOT` in their shell (profile, direnv, a foreground `dreamux serve`) while `config.json` stayed in `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/.dreamux` — `dreamux serve` and `dreamux daemon install` run from that shell now look for `config.json` under the exported root and fail on the same missing-file error (`dreamux doctor` reports it); and if the operator moves `config.json` there and re-runs `dreamux daemon install`, the shell's root is written into the unit, so the service moves to a root it never used: its durable state (dispatcher identities, Teams, Workflow runs, `access.json`) stays behind in the old root and the service comes up on a root that holds none of it. Rebuild: keep the root the old service actually used — do not assume it is the `DREAMUX_ROOT` your shell exports. (1) Find that root from the environment the old daemon actually ran with. For a managed service, read it from the running process (on Linux `tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/$(systemctl --user show -p MainPID --value dreamux)/environ | grep -E '^(DREAMUX_ROOT|HOME)='`) or, when it is not running, from everything that defines that environment: the installed unit and any drop-ins (`systemctl --user cat dreamux`), any `EnvironmentFile` they name, and the user manager's own environment (`systemctl --user show-environment`); on macOS, the plist `~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.excited.dreamux.plist` and `launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/dev.excited.dreamux`. A unit written by an earlier build has no `DREAMUX_ROOT` entry of its own, so unless one of those sources supplies it the root is `.dreamux` under the service's `HOME` (normally `~/.dreamux`). A foreground `dreamux serve` used the `DREAMUX_ROOT` of the shell that started it, else `~/.dreamux`. Confirm the root by checking that `<root>/state/` holds your dispatcher directories. (2) Put `config.json` at `<that root>/config.json`: move it from the old service's `DREAMUX_CONFIG_DIR` path (found the same way) when that names another directory (keep mode 0600, create parent directories as needed); there is nothing to move when it already sits in that root. (3) Re-run `dreamux daemon install` (or `dreamux onboard` again) from a shell whose `DREAMUX_ROOT` is that same root — or unset, when the root is `~/.dreamux` — so the unit is rewritten with the right `DREAMUX_ROOT`, then run `dreamux daemon restart`. For a foreground `dreamux serve`, export the same root in the shell that starts it. Only a deliberate change of root moves durable state: with the service stopped, move the old root's `state/` to `<new root>/state/` (`run/` is volatile, `cache/` is rebuildable, and `logs/` is diagnostics, so none of them needs to move) and `config.json` to `<new root>/config.json`, then do step (3) with `DREAMUX_ROOT` set to the new root; without the `state/` move the service starts on empty state.

PR #455 review round: `plugin/loader.ts`'s `constructPlugin` now validates a factory-returned plugin `name` against a safe single-segment pattern (1-64 ASCII letters/digits/dot/underscore/dash, starting with a letter or digit) and fails loading with `PluginLoadError` otherwise. `pluginStateDir` now uses `name` verbatim as the `state/plugins/<name>` directory segment instead of running it through the lossy teammate-name sanitizer, which mapped both `@acme/tool` and the unrelated `_acme_tool` to `state/plugins/_acme_tool` and passed `.`/`..` through unchanged (resolving up out of `state/plugins/`). Every built-in plugin name already conforms; a third-party `npm:` plugin whose factory returns a name outside this pattern now fails `dreamux serve` at load instead of silently sharing or escaping another plugin's state directory.

PR #455 review round, two scheduler fixes. `CronJobStore.parseCronJob` no longer fails loud on a leftover `deliver` field on an old cron-jobs.json job row: like the existing `dispatcher_id` tolerance, it is now an ordinary unknown field under the persisted-shape policy, ignored on load and dropped the next time that job is rewritten; `dreamux doctor` no longer names a store file for carrying it. Separately, a missed cron fire's rearm write no longer derives its `{ enabled, next_run_at }` write from the in-memory job snapshot `SchedulerService` captured before the fire; `CronJobStore.applyMissed` now derives that write from the row as it stands at write time, inside the store's own serialized update, so a `cron.update` committed while a fire's submission was in flight can no longer be silently overwritten by a stale missed-outcome write.

Core no longer rejects an Agent Runtime activity record whose `occurredAt` timestamp string is longer than 64 characters. This was the last provider-output length cap left over from R28 ("Core no longer re-validates an Agent Runtime provider's activity page against a byte/char/cursor-length budget", refactor-code-org-s2a-04); the provider's own bounds are the only bound now.

A `plugins[]` object entry (`{ ref, config }`) now follows the same persisted-shape policy (R21) as the rest of config.json: an unrecognized key alongside `ref`/`config` is tolerated and ignored instead of refusing `dreamux serve`. A missing `ref` still fails loading.

`dreamux uninstall` follows the existing next behavior: dry-run checks existence and reports planned removal without enumerating root contents or writing files; actual uninstall recursively removes the entire DREAMUX_ROOT, including other files and directories inside it. The foreign-retention predictor is removed. Results report removed or missing; permission and other filesystem errors still propagate, including after a successful preview. Normalized removal paths inside or containing a provider-derived operator runtime home are refused before any service mutation. Physical symlink aliases are not resolved. Current root addressing and service removal order remain unchanged.

`workflow_status` and `workflow_list` no longer serve a finished run's record from a stale in-memory cache for the rest of the dispatcher's process lifetime. The scope's `WorkflowRunStore` now releases a run's cached store once its owning run settles (or once a crash-recovery pass finds it already terminal), and reads finished records one-shot from disk afterward, so a hand edit to a finished run's record.json is now reflected.

A provider ref listed under the wrong kind in config.json (for example a `builtin:codex` agent-runtime provider referenced from a `channels[]` entry) now fails config validation with a `RuleViolation` naming the actual and expected kind, instead of the provider package loader's own contract error. This follows from built-in providers now registering their descriptor and implementation together as always-loaded plugins (R9): the mismatch is caught once, in config validation, for both built-in and `npm:` provider refs. No behavior change for a correctly configured install.
Code organization refactor stage 2a, item 3: cron jobs are no longer capped at 128 per dispatcher/Team owner. The cap had no named failure scenario. Old cron stores are unaffected.

Code organization refactor stage 2a, item 4: Core no longer re-validates an Agent Runtime provider's activity page against a byte/char/cursor-length budget, or a provider's declared capabilities against a tag-count/length or publicConfig size bound. The provider's own bounds are the only bound now.

Code organization refactor stage 2a, item 5: the `dispatcher.start` Command and the `dispatcher start` server-ctl CLI verb are removed. Every configured, enabled Dispatcher already starts automatically when the daemon starts; there was no supported way to stop one independently and restart it in-process to begin with.

Code organization refactor stage 2a, item 12 (R47): `dreamux serve` no longer runs its startup pre-flight that aggregated every dispatcher's pre-#233 leftover state and removed cron stores and aborted the whole process before the admin socket opened, and `dreamux doctor` no longer reports a dispatcher's leftover state as a row. A stale `channel-bindings.json`/`collaboration-spaces.json` at the dispatcher root, a pre-#233 flat `teammate/`/`team/` leaf (`records`, `turns`, `identities`, `history`, `sessions.jsonl`, `ledger`), or an agent identity record still carrying a removed field (`checkpoint`, `checkpoint_kind`, `session_ref`, `display_name`, `close_status`) are now silently ignored rather than triggering a fail-loud rebuild instruction. This is not `BREAKING:`: nothing an operator relied on to start stops working — the opposite failure mode (refusing to start) is what's removed. A cron store with an unrecognized version and an identity still keyed by the pre-#148 `provider_ref` format still raise a named error when actually read (a dispatcher's scheduler start, `dreamux doctor`'s unchanged cron rows), but that failure is no longer aggregated into a whole-process startup refusal — it now fails only the one dispatcher whose store or identity is affected, the same as any other per-dispatcher start failure.

Code organization refactor stage 4b item 1: moved AgentIdentityStore and AgentEntityCollectionStore onto TransactionalStore, deleted AgentRuntimeStateStore's own mutation tail in favor of the store's serialized update, and fixed four second-authority duplicate-reader sites (dispatcher-root identity shared between Dispatchers and DispatcherService, TeammateCollection.mustIdentity, reprepareDeletedManagedWorktree's nested-update pattern, and TeammateCollection.buildEntity minting a second, never-loaded AgentIdentityStore instead of reusing the one that created or read the entity). AgentIdentityStoreBinding no longer carries onPersisted; every create/update/upsert call now threads it explicitly. Named behavior change: a name lookup for a live TeamMate (mustIdentity) now answers from that TeamMate's own live identity instead of a fresh file read, so it can no longer race a runtime that just committed a status transition; record.json's shape is unchanged.

Code organization refactor stage 4b item 2: moved TeamStore onto a per-Team TransactionalStore, replacing its exclusive-write-plus-readback create path with a load-decide-write inside the store's own serialized queue and its manual write queue with the store's tail. TeamService now holds its Team's TransactionalStore handle directly instead of a caller-refreshed record field, and the Team read model answers leader_state from a live TeamService's own in-memory identity before falling back to a one-shot file read. record.json's shape, TeamStore's/TeamService's public methods, and Command/MCP-visible behavior are unchanged; only the anti-resurrection mechanism moved from 'merge against disk' to 'one in-memory owner per Team, merging against its committed value' (already an accepted operator ruling, 2026-09-19).

Code organization refactor stage 4b item 3: moved CronJobStore onto a single TransactionalStore<CronJobFile>, inlining the version-mismatch/missing-file-default check that JsonDocumentStore used to run. Dropped the operator-only nested `action` Command field from scheduler.cron.create/update. Its former `action.prompt` was consumed as the scheduled submission text; the Commands now take the same text as top-level `prompt`, while persisted jobs keep their internal `action.prompt` and stopped writing `dispatcher_id` in scheduler.cron.list/create/update/delete results, the cron_* MCP tool results, and newly written cron-jobs.json job rows; a leftover dispatcher_id on an old file now loads as an ordinary unknown field under the persisted-shape policy (tolerate unknown fields, reject only wrong types and missing fields) instead of being required and cross-checked against the store's own dispatcher id. Old cron-jobs.json files carrying either field still load. Named behavior change: deleting a Team's cron store file on dissolve now loads the file first (TransactionalStore.remove()'s own contract), so a cron-jobs.json that fails its version/shape check at that exact moment now fails the delete too, instead of always succeeding via a direct unlink(); this is one more of dissolve's ordinary collected cleanup-step failures, handled the same way as any other resource that would not close.

Code organization refactor stage 4b item 4: moved WorkflowRunStore onto a per-run TransactionalStore<WorkflowRunRecord | null>, inlining the version-mismatch/missing-file-default check that JsonDocumentStore used to run, and moved WorkflowJournal.create onto dreamux-utils' publishFileExclusive. run.ts keeps mutating its working draft before each persistence point; the queue that used to serialize those writes is gone (each run's own TransactionalStore now serializes them), but the reclassification of a failed journal/store write into WorkflowPersistenceError (which executeAgent's catch depends on to tell a storage failure apart from an ordinary agent failure) is preserved under a renamed helper. Named behavior change: WorkflowRun.snapshot(), which backs workflow_status/workflow_list for a live run, now returns the run's last committed (written) value instead of the in-progress in-memory draft between a mutation and the write that persists it. Freshness here was already documented as unspecified, so this narrows rather than changes the contract, but it is a real, observable difference from today's snapshot timing. record.json's shape, the journal's shape, and every public method signature are unchanged. `this.record.x = …` in-place mutation and `AgentCall.record` as a live alias into `this.record.agents[]` were both kept as they were, rather than becoming a pure builder passed to `store.update()` and an index respectively; traced for data loss (each write clones at commit time and every store now serializes on its own `TransactionalStore` queue) and found none.

Code organization refactor stage 4b item 5: config.json now tolerates unknown top-level, dispatchers[], channels[], agents[], and dispatchers[].workspace keys instead of rejecting them; wrong types and missing required fields are still rejected. Per R21's tolerate-unknown-fields policy, this also removes every remaining named rejection of a retired config.json key: the top-level codex block, dispatchers[].runtime, the dispatchers[].feishu/.codex legacy-shape pre-check, and channels[].collaborationSpace are no longer special-cased and now load as ordinary tolerated unknown fields like any other retired key.

Code organization refactor stage 4c: added two Commands, config.agents.get and config.agents.replace, reachable through admin.sock and any Channel's in-process invoke port like every other Command. config.agents.get returns the current agents[] in file shape with every secret-named value emptied; config.agents.replace validates and writes a whole new agents[] array, matched to the existing one by id (submitting an empty secret-named value keeps the stored value). A replace takes effect for the next runtime launch only — a runtime already running keeps what it launched with. The first replace re-serializes config.json with two-space indentation and the submitted agent order; other values, and dispatchers[], are written unchanged. Neither Command is dispatcher-scoped, and dispatchers[] still has no Command. No persisted-format change.
team.history's grep filter now ignores leading/trailing whitespace in the search term, matching teammate.history's existing behavior.

Code organization refactor stage 6a item 2a: renamed the class service/agent/service.ts's TeammateService -> AgentService and service/agent/runtime-generation.ts's TeammateRuntimeOwner -> RuntimeGeneration (propagated to every consumer's type-only imports across the package, e.g. dispatcher-service/ and team-service/; service/agent/factory.ts is left on the old name, since converting it into the per-dispatcher AgentServiceFactory is stage 6a item 2b). This one class now serves three roles (the Dispatcher's own Agent, a Team's leader, and an ordinary TeamMate) but hardcoded 'TeamMate' in every thrown-error message regardless of which role it was closing, locking, or starting; a Team's leader.close() (dissolve) or a Dispatcher agent's runtime-generation failure produced a wrong 'TeamMate ...' message. Added agentRoleNoun(role, name) (service/agent/service-types.ts, to avoid a service.ts <-> runtime-generation.ts import cycle) and used it at every such error message in these two files, so a Dispatcher agent now reads 'the Dispatcher agent ...' and a Team's leader reads 'Team leader "<name>" ...'. Most of an ordinary TeamMate's own wording is unchanged (byte-identical, same JSON.stringify(name) quoting); four messages that previously named 'TeamMate' without the entity's name now include it for every role, including teammate, as a byproduct of routing through the one shared helper: the close-note validation message (this is also a real fix, not just wording -- close() runs on a Team's leader too on dissolve, per team-service/closing.ts, so the pre-existing text was already wrong there), the two closed-with-no-closed_at invariant-violation messages, and the stale-lock-token invariant-violation message. Also deleted two dead-by-construction fields: ownsWorktreeOnClose (its condition, restricted to the three real construction sites, was already exactly implied by identity.worktree.mode === 'managed' && identity.worktree.cleanup === 'delete-on-close' alone -- the Dispatcher agent and every Team leader are always worktree.mode 'reuse-cwd', and a Team-scoped TeamMate's spawn path always forces a reuse-cwd shared workspace, so the flag never disagreed with the identity's own facts since it was introduced) and assertIdentityScope plus runtime-id.ts's three assert*Scope helper functions (the identity was already read by a store scoped to the correct directory by the owner that materialized it, so re-checking scope on every ensureStarted() call had no failure scenario construction-time scoping doesn't already rule out). No persisted format, public API, or MCP/Command contract changed.

Code organization refactor stage 6a item 3: the completion notice the Dispatcher's own agent receives after one of its Team's leaders settles a team.create-with-prompt turn (R16, deliverCompletionToDispatcher) always read 'TeamMate <name> has finished its task,' misdescribing a Team leader as a TeamMate. Added role: TeammateRole to TeammateCompletionFact (service/completion-router/index.ts) and threaded the producing AgentService's own role (fixed for its lifetime, passed once into EntityTurnCoordinatorOptions at construction) through service/agent/turn.ts's fact construction. service/agent/completion-renderer.ts's teammateStatusLine now words the sentence by the producer's actual role: a Team leader completion reads 'Team leader <name> has finished its task.' (and failed/stopped variants); an ordinary TeamMate completion, the only other role a delivered completion is produced by today, is unchanged. The Dispatcher-role branch is exhaustive but currently unreached -- the Dispatcher's own agent never attaches a completion-delivery closure to its own turns today, so 'The Dispatcher agent has finished its task.' is not yet observable, but is now correctly worded for when it is. workflowStatusLine is untouched. No persisted format, public API, or MCP/Command contract changed.

Code organization refactor stage 6a item 4: deleted TeammateRuntimeOwnerCallbacks, the function-valued dependency bag RuntimeGeneration used to reach back into AgentService's private phase field via isActive()/markClosing(). RuntimeGeneration.ensureStarted() now takes no phase callback and simply resolves once the runtime is live or throws; it no longer self-aborts mid-launch. AgentService now owns the race check itself through one new private method, ensureRuntimeStarted(), used by every one of its three callers of runtimeGeneration.ensureStarted() (admitToRuntime, activate(), the locked Workflow submit path): it checks this.phase itself before calling ensureStarted() (replacing the old pre-lease isActive() check) and again immediately after ensureStarted() resolves, stopping the runtime and reporting not-active itself when a close raced and won the awaited start (replacing the old post-start isActive() self-abort). The one case that used to call markClosing() — startFromRecord's rollback branch where the rollback's own runtime.stop() also fails after a native start failure — now has RuntimeGeneration throw a new named error, RuntimeTerminationUnproven (an AggregateError subclass carrying the same start/stop failure pair), which ensureRuntimeStarted() catches to set AgentService's own phase to 'closing' before rethrowing; this is the mutation every caller previously got for free via the callback, so centralizing it is what keeps a runtime whose termination could not be proven from being handed out by a later ensureStarted() call, which treats any non-null runtime handle as already live and never re-examines it. Internal control-flow refactor moving which class owns a phase decision. One caller-visible admission-outcome shape changed for the narrow start-races-close window: a submission that used to reject with an 'is closing' Error now resolves as an ordinary {status:'stopped'} TurnAdmission (the same shape a submission to an already-stopped recipient always gets), so its display reason becomes 'the agent runtime is not running' instead of the old message text. The issue #63 non-blocking submit ordering (runtime.submit fires synchronously before being handed to the admission continuation queue) is untouched.

Code organization refactor stage 6b item 2 (R48): deleted the team.hooks.created plugin hook end-to-end, together with its background scheduling (fireCreated), its InFlightWork-backed in-flight tracking, and the Dispatcher shutdown drain that awaited it. A plugin that tapped this hook loses it; nothing in this tree taps it today, and Dispatcher shutdown no longer waits on it.

Fixed a bug: team.create with a prompt, called through admin.sock or a Channel's team.create Command, no longer pushes the leader's first-turn completion back to the Dispatcher Agent -- only the Dispatcher's own team MCP create tool call does now, matching the deliverCompletionToDispatcher contract team.submit has always had. DispatcherService.createTeam, TeamCollection.createFromRequest/createAtCandidate, and TeamService.createNew all take an explicit deliverCompletionToDispatcher boolean threaded the same way teamId/payloadHash already thread through; service/team/commands.ts's create.execute() passes false, service/team/mcp.ts's create() (the Dispatcher's own MCP call) passes true. initial-prompt.ts's submitInitialLeaderPrompt is folded into TeamService.createNew, which now calls submitToLeader(...) directly and checks the returned TurnAdmission itself, so the initial turn runs through the same admit-fenced submission path (and the same completion-initiator wiring) as every later turn; resolveTeamLeaderCompletionDelivery (completion-targets.ts) is deleted as the second initiator-to-delivery mapping it duplicated. TeamLeaderCompletionTargets itself, used for a Team's own members' completions reporting to the leader, is unrelated and unchanged.

Code organization refactor stage 6b item 6 (R10): rewrote TeamClosing's dissolve/close sequence. TeamClosingDeps drops the leader()/closeLeaderForDissolve() callback pair; dissolve(input, leader), abandonCreation(input, leader), and stopForHost(leader) now all take the TeamLeader as a plain AgentService | null value, read once by TeamService (its own leader_ field) at each call site instead of asked for through a callback. stopChildRuntimesForDissolve and the child-stopping half of stopRuntimesForDissolve are unified as stopChildrenForDissolve() and stopAllForDissolve(leader), both still built on the one shared, non-throwing stopChildRuntimes(failures) helper so a member-stop failure and a leader-stop failure still aggregate into one thrown error exactly as today; closeResources (now closeChildren) drops its own redundant repeat of workflows.closeAdmission()/stopAll() and scheduler.stop() -- both were already covered, idempotently, by stopAllForDissolve immediately before it, so the repeat inside closeResources answered nothing new. abandonCreation's adoptDurableLeader callback is removed: TeamService.createNew's own catch adopts an orphaned durable leader itself, before calling abandonCreation, and passes the result as the leader argument; a failure during that adoption attempt is now logged rather than folded into the thrown AggregateError alongside the original creation-failure cause. The number, order, and gating of every worktree assessment, the dissolve refusal contract, the dissolve receipt shape, and team.closed timing are unchanged. TeamService forgets this.leader_ (checked once, after closing.dissolve() settles) whenever the new AgentService.isSafeToForget() is true, not only once AgentService.isRetired() confirms the close's own durable write also landed: a leader whose close() fully released runtime authority (stopRuntime() succeeded) but whose identity write then failed is still forgotten and rebuilt fresh from disk on next use, matching the pre-refactor unconditional pre-close null. isSafeToForget() stays false for the different case of an unproven runtime termination (a failed start whose own rollback stop could not prove the native runtime dead), because that runtime might still be alive and must not be silently forgotten. A leader whose close was never reached at all (an earlier stop or assessment refused first) is left live and reusable exactly as before.

workflow.run and the workflow_run MCP tool now report BAD_REQUEST instead of INTERNAL for an empty resolved script, a scriptPath that is not a regular file, or a scriptPath over the read-size cap -- each is the caller's own mistake, not a server failure. Missing script/scriptPath and an out-of-range max_concurrency already reported BAD_REQUEST and are unaffected.

dispatcher.submit and team.submit now report SUBMIT_FAILED / SUBMIT_AMBIGUOUS instead of TEAM_SUBMIT_FAILED / TEAM_SUBMIT_AMBIGUOUS for a failed or ambiguous submission. The shared submit receipt covers both callers, and a Dispatcher's own Agent submission has no Team involved, so the wire code no longer names Team.

A dispatcher's own admission gate and its workflow-run admission check now report SERVER_SHUTTING_DOWN instead of INTERNAL when they refuse a request, matching the code the process-wide shutdown fence and a dispatcher's Channel port already reported for their own closed-scope refusals.

ChannelService.closeAll() now collects and reports every channel session's close failure instead of logging and swallowing it. A Dispatcher's own close already wraps this call in its aggregate shutdown-failure collector, so a channel provider's close() throwing during a dispatcher stop or the daemon's graceful shutdown now surfaces as a shutdown failure where it was previously silent.

dispatcher.status's status field and each dispatcher.list entry's status field now always report the runtime vocabulary (declared/starting/ready/degraded/stopping/stopped). Previously dispatcher.list reported the identity vocabulary (starting/running/degraded/closed/stopped) for both a live and a cold dispatcher, and dispatcher.status mixed the two: the runtime vocabulary while live, the identity vocabulary while cold. A caller branching on 'running' or 'closed' needs to branch on 'ready' or 'stopped' instead. Two cases that previously reported 'stopped' now report 'declared': a dispatcher with no persisted identity yet, and a materialized dispatcher whose agent is built but has never activated its runtime in this process (previously this fell back to the persisted identity's status, which could be stale after a crash).

team.status already refused during a dispatcher stop; team.history and team.list now refuse the same way (SERVER_SHUTTING_DOWN) instead of answering from a Team's stale records. All three are per-Team operational reads and are now gated uniformly; dispatcher.list, dispatcher.status, and channel.list are unaffected and remain observable through a stop.

TeammateCollection now takes its admission fence at construction and gates every TeammateOps verb (spawn/send/close/list/status/history/last/getCapabilities) internally, uniformly, instead of wrapping only the three mutating verbs at the dispatcher-service boundary. A dispatcher-root teammate.list/.status/.history/.last call now refuses with SERVER_SHUTTING_DOWN during a Dispatcher stop instead of answering from stale records; a Team-scoped one now refuses with TEAM_CLOSED during that Team's dissolve, and with SERVER_SHUTTING_DOWN during a Dispatcher stop, instead of always answering. dispatcher-service/teammate-ops.ts is deleted; DispatcherService.teammates returns the collection directly.

The `dreamux dispatcher start` CLI verb is removed (R11: no in-process restart after a dispatcher has closed). It never reached a working code path (no `'start'` case existed on the server-side dispatcher-control method resolver), but its removal is a CLI surface change an operator's script could still reference. `dreamux dispatcher status`/`list` are unaffected.

A dispatcher's shutdown stops Workflows, each Team, each materialized TeamMate runtime, and the dispatcher's own Agent runtime, joins every already-admitted operation, then repeats that same runtime sweep once more before closing Channels last. The sweep runs before the admitted-work join as well as after: an admitted call can itself be starting a runtime with no timeout of its own, so joining first would wait on exactly the runtime the sweep exists to stop, and stopping it first is what makes that runtime's own teardown unblock the join. The second, post-join pass catches a pre-fence admission that only starts - or, since a runtime stop fences an entity's admission for its own convergence only and never durably closes it, revives - a runtime after the first pass already read past that entity. Separately, TeammateCollection's and TeamCollection's own entity-construction paths check the dispatcher's closing fact the instant they register a brand-new entity and self-close its runtime immediately, preempting a spawned TeamMate's first submission outright (a Team's leader can already have taken its first prompt by the time the collection notices, so it only stops that runtime as soon as it can) - a different race, from a new entity's own construction, than the two-pass sweep covers.

Plugin hook review fixes: a plugin's own interceptor added with `hook.intercept` — on `call`, `tap`, `loop`, `result`, `done`, `error`, or `register` — is guarded the same way a tap is, attributed to the plugin that registered it: on `dispatcher`, `team`, and a launch hook a throw is logged and skipped, and on `hooks.plugin.for(name)` a throw fails plugin loading with a clear error, so neither crashes `dreamux serve` or `dreamux doctor` — including a `done`/`error` interceptor on an async hook, which tapable invokes from a continuation an ordinary try/catch around the hook cannot see. Interceptor methods must be synchronous: an `async` one's rejection is logged at runtime and fails plugin loading on `hooks.plugin.for(name)` with an error naming the interceptor, and an `async` `register` leaves the tap unchanged. A launch-hook interceptor sees only an opaque, disconnected handle, never the internal launch draft, so it cannot add a skill root that skips the skill fence. An async plugin tap on the sync `dispatcher`/`team` hooks is logged and skipped, with no unhandled rejection risk. An async `server()` or `contribute()` fails loading with a clear error naming the plugin, so a tap registered after its first `await` is never silently lost. A `plugins[]` entry's `config` block for a plugin with no `config.read` is ignored, so `dreamux serve` starts.

patch.comment: Release fully retired Team stores and read historical records from disk while preserving live owners, queued writes and cleanup. Keep an admitted leader dissolve on that captured owner through its asynchronous precheck and detached cleanup, even when initial construction fails. Restore non-blocking Codex inbound and final-parent behavioral coverage with explicit native-model opt-in and separate auth-free protocol checks. Retain revocable event sources and skip display DTO production without an audience while preserving durable observations. Restore actual ESLint code-line limits and public package boundary assertions. Ignore non-Team inventory names without reading or altering their contents, and keep one construction record acquisition through workspace preparation and publication. Pure retained-record reads return the committed snapshot without waiting for unrelated queued writes; writer releases still drain their captured queues.

`dreamux serve` now always exits on SIGTERM or SIGINT: a shutdown that fails is logged and the process exits with status 1, and a shutdown that has not settled by a fixed deadline is cut off and the process exits with status 1, where a failed shutdown used to leave the process running. Under systemd (`Restart=on-failure`), a failed or cut-off shutdown that was not requested through `systemctl stop` therefore restarts the service, and a runtime child process can outlive a daemon cut off this way, as after a manager kill. A value refused by config validation in an online config replace is now reported as a bad request rather than an internal failure. An unknown `builtin:` provider ref in a replace payload is classified the same way, and its message no longer reads as an external-provider load failure; `serve`, `doctor` and `onboard` print the same reworded message for such a ref. The `repo` input of Dispatcher `spawn` and Team `create` carries its field descriptions and length bounds, defined once beside the repo request reader; because the canonical `spawn` and `team.create` commands validate against that same schema, an empty or over-long repo path, base ref or branch is now rejected as a bad request over the admin socket and the Channel port as well. `last` on a running agent, including a TeamMate a `send` is still reopening, reads the provider, config and session of the runtime that is running instead of the current config. Two lifecycle fixes: a Workflow handle lock taken while an agent is created is released when that agent closes before the handle is handed over, and looking up an absent Team no longer leaves a store cached for that id.

Preserve existing taps when a plugin register interceptor omits its result. Reject asynchronous plugin factories and config readers with attributed load errors while observing their rejections. Reject simultaneously loaded plugin names that differ only by ASCII case; preserve the spelling of individual names, API keys, and state paths.
Bind fixed runtime context once and return persistence and cleanup operations to their owning services.

Team dissolve now writes the record closed immediately after its worktree precheck passes, then destroys every child service (Workflows, scheduler, members, leader) and reclaims the worktree as best-effort steps behind that commit, instead of stopping and closing children first and writing closed last. A member that dirties the managed worktree after the precheck no longer refuses the dissolve: the Team still closes, and a non-forced cleanup then only keeps the directory instead of removing it. A process that dies after the closed record lands now leaves the Team durably closed with whatever children the destroy pass had not yet reached, rather than reopening it. Persisted record shapes are unchanged.

A workflow status/list read or a cron list made while its dispatcher is stopping or its Team is dissolving is now refused instead of answered: WorkflowService and SchedulerService fence those reads behind the same admission gate their mutations already crossed. A leader-scoped mutation racing both a dispatcher stop and a Team dissolve at the same time now reports TeamClosedError instead of ServerShuttingDownError, now that the TeamLeader handle is assembled from surfaces that already fence themselves instead of forwarding through 12 hand-written closures. Internally, several resources a parent used to build and hand down (the Workflow journal, the Agent admission ledger, the per-Team record handle) are now built by the module that owns them instead; persisted record and config shapes are unchanged.

BREAKING: Rebuild: if a cron store carries a removed shape, delete that job — or the whole `cron-jobs.json` under `~/.dreamux/state/<dispatcher-id>/` or `~/.dreamux/state/<dispatcher-id>/team/<team-id>/` — and recreate the schedule with `cron_create`. Every agent-facing tool failure and every admin/Channel command failure now produces a result the caller can act on. A failure a domain knows about states its own stable code, the concrete fact, and the next step to take: a Team that is gone (TEAM_NOT_FOUND) or over (TEAM_CLOSED) — now two distinct answers on every surface, including a TeamLeader's own — a TeamMate that does not exist (TEAMMATE_NOT_FOUND), a cron job id that names nothing (CRON_JOB_NOT_FOUND), and an unknown workflow run (WORKFLOW_RUN_NOT_FOUND). A caller mistake is reported as BAD_REQUEST naming the rule it broke: a malformed cron expression, an unusable timezone, an invalid Team or TeamMate name, a blank name_prefix, intent, or close note, an unusable history limit, and an unreadable history cursor. These codes now reach admin.sock and Channel callers, where such failures previously reported INTERNAL, and the next step travels beside the code and message as a new optional `action` field on the admin error envelope and on a rejected in-process Channel command. Only a domain's own named rule becomes BAD_REQUEST: an unforeseen failure raised while validating a request, and any rule broken by persisted state, stay unclassified. An unclassified failure is no longer answered with fixed sanitized text and is no longer wrapped on its way out: it reaches the caller as INTERNAL carrying the message it already had, and is logged whole — stack included — by the boundary that observed it. A malformed MCP delegate result now fails `mcp.toolcall` instead of being reported as a successful one. Closing an already-closed TeamMate is reported as the success it is — including when a concurrent close commits while this one is reading — rather than as a failure. An admin socket that is absent or refusing is now reported as TRANSPORT_ERROR carrying the socket error Node itself reported, instead of the authored "is the server running?" advice that replaced it. No config, state, or path shape changed and no rebuild is required.

BREAKING: Review: watch one conversation card end-to-end after upgrading. An input now appears on the card at the moment it is submitted rather than after the runtime accepted it; a submission that never reaches a runtime now ends the recipient's one open card with the failure text; and a completion push-back whose recipient's runtime disappears between the moment it is prepared and the moment it is submitted is now visible (the delivered body plus a failed end naming the reason) where it used to be silently dropped — a push-back to a recipient already known to be stopped is still refused before anything is published and stays as silent as it was. No config, state, cache, or path shape changed and no rebuild is needed. Core's conversation projection is keyed on the Agent: `projectSubmitted`/`projectSettled`/`projectNativeTurnEnd` collapse into `projectInput`/`projectActivity`, which are fail-open by contract. `EntityTurnCoordinator` carries no display code at all — its two sinks, the `RuntimeSubmission`-keyed turn map, the 512-entry early-activity buffer, and the per-submission activity dedupe are deleted — and `EntityTurn` drops the five fields only display read. Every admission that produces no turn — stopped, skipped, ambiguous, or failed — ends its display as `failed` with the reason attached. `TeammateService` has one `runtime.submit` call site: a completion push-back is the ordinary admitted input asking `{ wake: false }`. The Core event seal's catalog is now a total record over the event union, so an unlisted kind fails to compile instead of being dropped at runtime.

A runtime that cannot start now surfaces on the first message's display instead of failing `team.create`.

A TeamLeader whose Agent Runtime fails to start now shows the submitted input and the provider's own error on its conversation display, instead of leaving the display open on its opening label. The leader's runtime starts inside the submission that needs it on every TeamLeader path (Channel, Agent delegate, cron), and a `starting` Team becomes `running` once its leader has taken a turn.

Give the scheduler one definition of a valid cron schedule. Two consequences a reader may notice: a corrupt-state report for an unknown timezone now says which timezone was rejected instead of relaying the platform's wording, and a genuine platform fault during the timezone probe is no longer misreported as corrupt state. Add .agents/reference/release-process.md SOP page and link it from .agents/root.md. The new doc records the 4-stage development-and-release pipeline (PR to next -> alpha prerelease -> automatic beta prerelease on push to next -> one-click promote-next driving fast-forward to main + version bump + topology repair + stable publish), the strict main-is-strict-prefix-of-next invariant, the release/topology coupling design choices (GITHUB_TOKEN anti-loop guard -> explicit dispatch; version-bump commit on main -> sync-next step), and a failure-mode recovery table. Operators now have a single source of truth for how code enters the repo, moves through prereleases, and ships to npm latest. No package surface changes.

Bugfix for the promote-next workflow: the `git push origin main` in promote-next.yml uses the default GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub's documented anti-infinite-loop guard deliberately prevents a GITHUB_TOKEN-originated push from re-triggering other workflows. As a result, the `on.push.main` trigger in release.yml silently did not fire after a successful promote, requiring a manual dispatch workaround. Fix: (1) grant `permissions.actions:write`, (2) add a final `gh workflow run release.yml --ref main` step that dispatches the stable release pipeline explicitly after each non-noop promote, (3) update the workflow header comments to document the real coupling. No published package surface changes; this is a release-process workflow robustness fix.

Add a new 'sync next onto the freshly bumped main' step at the end of the release.yml version job. The long-lived topology invariant between the two long-lived branches is: 'main must always be a strict ancestor of next' (promote-next.yml enforces this with a hard fail). Without this step, every successful stable release breaks the invariant: the version job writes a 'chore(release): version packages [skip ci]' commit directly to main without going through next, which forces the next promote-next run into Topology Violation and requires a manual rebuild of the next branch (cherry-pick + force push). The new step fast-forwards next onto the freshly bumped main SHA immediately after the version bump, keeping the invariant alive. Skip logic: sync only if next still points at the exact pre-bump SHA; otherwise next already moved on and will absorb the bump via a future promote-next. No published package surface changes.
